body.statement: Uniformly over the finite slices \(P_n\in\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\) induced by complete arrays in \(\mathfrak M^{\mathrm{CY}}\), the eligible-cohort estimator satisfies \[D_n^{-1}(\widehat\tau-\tau^{\mathrm{event}})=\left(\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}e_q/\sigma_q\right)_{k\in\mathcal K_n}+\rho_n,\qquad \|\rho_n\|_\infty=O_{P_n}(\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K)).\] The coefficients are obtained by aggregating the exact Choi--Yuan Proposition A.4 block coefficients with eligible-unit weights \(n_g/N_k\) before any covariance calculation.
body.justification: This is the missing bridge from scalar block debiasing to one growing adoption-aligned event process.
body.gap: Choi and Yuan, Proposition A.4 and their staggered-adoption theorem, give block or scalar expansions but do not aggregate an increasing number of event horizons uniformly.
body.consumer: It supplies the vector score needed to attach whole-curve uncertainty to the Ben-Michael--Feller right-to-carry event plot.

obligation.what_is_open: A simultaneous Choi--Yuan block expansion whose nonlinear errors obey \( |r_{gk}|\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) for every eligible \( (g,k)\) on one event with probability tending to one uniformly over \(\mathcal M_n^{\mathrm{CY}}\).
obligation.obstruction: The definition of \(\rho_n\) proves the vector equality but not its stochastic rate.  The frozen core contains only a bibliographic description of Proposition A.4, not a declared cited theorem with a growing-block simultaneous probability bound.  Scalar or blockwise \(O_P\) control does not imply control of a maximum over a growing collection.
obligation.attempted: Expanded the eligible-unit aggregation before taking maxima and reduced the target rate to one explicit simultaneous block-remainder event.  Checked the relevant frozen bibliography record; it supplies provenance but no theorem statement or tail probability from which the required union can be proved.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact vector equality is already forced by the definition of
\(\rho_n\).  Indeed, because
\(a_{kq}=c_{kq}\sigma_q/s_k\),
\[
\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}a_{kq}\frac{e_q}{\sigma_q}
=s_k^{-1}\sum_{q\in\mathcal Q_n^{\mathrm{IF}}}c_{kq}e_q,
\]
and rearranging the definition of \(\rho_{n,k}\) gives the asserted
coordinate equality.  To isolate the missing step, let \(r_{gk}\) denote
the nonlinear remainder in the exact debiased expansion for block
\((g,k)\).  Cohort aggregation would give
\[
\rho_{n,k}=s_k^{-1}\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}r_{gk}.
\]
Consequently, on any event on which
\(\lvert r_{gk}\rvert\le C R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}\) simultaneously for
all eligible \((g,k)\),
\[
\|\rho_n\|_\infty
\le C\max_{k\in\mathcal K_n}s_k^{-1}
\sum_{g\in E_k}\frac{n_g}{N_k}R_{gk}^{\mathrm{CY}}
=C\Delta_{\mathrm{CY},n}(K).
\]
Thus the desired rate follows from, and is reduced exactly to, a
simultaneous block-remainder event with probability tending to one
uniformly over the finite slices.  No such event is a frozen assumption
or established statement.
